descriptionMarkdown:
Inspired by DocJade's [Autorail](https://factorioprints.com/view/-O9VRJfQs93GnPuihM2B) and mods like LTN, and using its included rail segments.

This BP book allows for automatic dispatching of trains from provider to requester stations, similar to LTN or Project Cybersyn, but in vanilla. The system is very feature-complete, and functions almost at the level of the actual mods, minus just a few features and limitations.

### Features
 - Completely automatic dispatching
 - Items and fluids supported
 - Depot bypass
 - Dispatching multiple trains at once (with configurable max train limit)


### Limitations
 - Not flexible with train layouts`*`
 - Can't request partial train loads
 - Need a base-wide circuit line for each train type (only 2 types of trains at a time unless you run multiple separate lines)

`*`Only some layouts are provided. More can be generated - see the "Train Layouts" section

### Usage
1. Add the global clock to your network, connecting the red and green wires
2. Add at least 1 depot and refueler to your train network
3. Add a provider and requester station (keeping in mind to select item or fluid), following the prompts. 
   - Connect the corresponding wire color (from the book it lies under. Adding the opposite color has no effect, so you can connect both if you would like) on the big power pole to the network
   - Place a loader/unloader, or attach the correct wire (from the parent book) to all storages for the station. Optionally, the opposite color wire on requester stations carries the item signal for inserter filtering.
4. Add at least one DragonTrain of the correct type

**Note:** In order for station IDs to be assigned properly, connect stations one at a time to the network. For instance, connect station 1 to the network, then station 2, rather than connecting station 1 and 2 together, then both to the network. This prevents a stampeding problem of multiple trains accepting the same request.

### Train Layouts
Several train layouts are provided in this BP. If you want any more, this is where it starts to get a little more complicated (but cool!)
Because of the nature of this system, lots of information is in the blueprints that is dependent on the amount of wagons and names of stations that cant be encoded in BP parameterization. In order to get around this, I am programmatically generating train layout BPs with this information. To make your own custom DragonTrain BP with any layouts, take a look at my [GitHub repo](https://github.com/DragonDuck24/DragonTrainFactorio) for the project, where you can set any variants and generate the full BP book.

### How It Works
Requester stations send a signal to the circuit network for the amount of train loads of the item, along with setting the train limit to that value. Provider stations simply set their train limit to the number of train loads of the item that it is able to supply with current inventory. Both stations detect the amount of inbound trains and subtract that amount from the requested total of that item, in order to prevent too many trains of that item being dispatched. All stations carry the currently requested train loads of items, so that any train leaving a station is able to detect outstanding requests in order to make a delivery through an interrupt. To prevent all trains accepting a request on the same tick, stations are assigned an ID upon connection to the network. The global clock cycles through these IDs, and a train can only accept a request if their station's ID is currently selected on the clock.

### Issues and questions
Use the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/DragonDuck24/DragonTrainFactorio) to report any issues you may find. If you have any questions about usage, the layout generation, or want more detail into the inner workings, reach out to me on discord, username dragonduck24
